manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the blackboard eraser and throw it into the trash bin.

Task description: The target is the rectangular blackboard eraser to the left of the mouse, with a black top and light-colored bottom edge. Pick it up and put it into the trash can lined with a black bag.

Success criteria: The blackboard eraser has been picked up from the table and released inside the trash bin, not left on the rim or caught on the trash-bag edge.

## Execution tips

- Span the eraser's short dimension and grip straight middle sections of its long edges with an opening slightly greater than the grasp width. This reduces slipping from inadequate end contact; also avoid the nearby pen and mouse.
- The gripper partly obscures the eraser. Before closing, use visible side edges or a slight viewpoint adjustment to confirm fingers on opposite sides rather than image overlap while actually pressing the top.
- When carrying the blackboard eraser toward the bin, keep both its bottom and fingertips above the rim with clearance to avoid hitting the bin wall or catching the turned-out trash bag.
- Release in a spacious area inside the bin opening with the eraser's full outline within the boundary, avoiding bag folds. A short drop reduces rim impacts, bounce-outs, or snagging on the bag.

I read the returned manual and confirmed that the target is the blackboard eraser to the left of the mouse, with the bin on the right. Only the right arm is available. I am adjusting the grasp angle and using the wrist camera to confirm the fingers' position relative to the eraser.

An orientation adjustment reached a controller motion limit; the tool returned a recoverable state. I changed the approach path using actual position. The right arm now moves normally and the entire eraser is visible.

The gripper is aligned with the eraser's long edges and descending in steps no larger than 1 cm. After closing, I will make a small test lift to confirm it leaves the table with the gripper before transferring to the bin.

The blackboard eraser lifted with the gripper and remained stable relative to it during continuous observation; the actual gripper opening is about 47 mm. I will raise it first, leaving enough clearance to get over the bin rim.
The grasp remains stable, and the gripper is about 37.5 cm high and moving above the bin. Near the mouth, I will shorten steps and confirm the whole eraser is inside the opening before release.

The blackboard eraser is stable and is passing over the left edge of the trash bin. There is still height clearance, and I am moving inward toward the opening in steps of 1 cm while avoiding the folded-over trash bag.

The blackboard eraser has been moved above the inside of the bin opening, with no visible slipping or rim contact. I will make a small pose adjustment to recheck the drop location, then release and observe.

The gripper is fully open; the board eraser has detached and disappeared inside the bin opening, with no visible resting on the rim or bag mouth. Observations indicate the drop is complete; the on-site operator must confirm its final position inside. I will now end this episode.
